pictures.c: Map showing the main geological, geomorphological and tectonic features of the area North of the Fucino basin. Notice that the slip vectors along the OPF are dip-slip with a slight left-lateral component of motion (from Piccardi et al. [1999]).

Top: constraints on the timing of  the two most recent paleoearthquakes. Bottom: map of largest historical earthquakes suggesting the existence of a gap coincident with the OPF (from Pantosti et al. [1996]).

pictures.t: Map of Campo Porcaro trench site
pictures.c: Detailed topographic map of site C at Campo Porcaro. The figure shows the location of trenches and the trace of topographic profiles (from D'Addezio et al. [1996]).
Geological and geomorphological map of Piano di Pezza. The figure shows the fault scarp and the location of three exploratory trenches (from Pantosti et al. [1996]).

pictures.t: Photo of Piano di Pezza scarp
pictures.c: Ovindoli-Pezza fault scarp cutting a modern alluvial fan along the northern margin of Piano di Pezza. The location is reported in the general map as Site A. Photo by D. Pantosti.
Topographic profiles across the main and antithetic fault scarps at Campo Porcaro (from D'Addezio et al. [1996]). See general map for the exact location.

pictures.t: Structural map of the Fucino basin and surroundings
pictures.c: Seismotectonic map showing the trace of the Ovindoli-Pezza fault system, major active faults of the area and distribution of recent seismicity. The surface breaks of the 1915 earthquake are highlighted by dots (from Piccardi et al. [1999]).

Structural evolution of the Fucino basin and surroundings according to Galadini [1999]. This model proposes that activity of the OPF began in the Middle Pleistocene with left-lateral kinematics. From Galadini [1999].

pictures.t: Log of Trench 1 at Piano di Pezza
pictures.c: Detailed log of Trench 1 excavated across the Ovindoli-Pezza fault scarp at site A. At least two paleoevents can be identified in the sequence. Triangles indicate the location of dated samples (from Pantosti et al. [1996]).

pictures.t: Photo of Trench 1 at Piano di Pezza
pictures.c: View of the south-east wall of Trench 1. The arrows indicate the Piano di Pezza fault scarp. The numbers indicate the different units of the stratigraphic sequence (same as in corresponding trench log) (from Pantosti et al. [1996]).

pictures.t: Log of Trench 3 at Piano di Pezza
pictures.c: Schematic log and graphic reconstruction of trench 3 (site B), obtained by removing the deformation produced by the two events identified in the trench (from Pantosti et al. [1996]).

pictures.t: Photo of Trench 3 at Piano di Pezza
pictures.c: View of the southeast wall of Trench 3. The main fault zone is outlined by red lines. Numbers indicate the various units of the stratigraphic sequence (same as in trench log). Photo by D. Pantosti.

pictures.t: Photo of Trench 4 at Piano di Pezza
pictures.c: Simplified log of trench 4 (site C, Campo Porcaro) and view of the south wall of the trench showing the main fault zone and the small graben that formed in front of it (from D'Addezio et al. [1996]).

pictures.t: Regional evolution of the Liri, Fucino and L'Aquila basins
pictures.c: Deformation evolution of the Abruzzi region. According to this model, beginning with Early Pleistocene times, the bending of the compressive margin caused left-lateral strike-slip kinematics along N160- to NS-striking faults (from Galadini [1999]).

pictures.t: General tectonic map of the area
pictures.c: Simplified tectonic map of Ovindoli-Pezza Fault and surrounding areas (from Pantosti et al. [1996]).

pictures.t: Surface traces of active or potentially active faults in central Italy
pictures.c: A number of surface active or potentially active faults identified and mapped by Bosi (1975) in a large region stretching from the Apennines piedmont east of Rome to the Adriatic coast  (Vannoli et al., [2012])

pictures.t: Surface normal faults and their slip directions in central Italy
pictures.c: Surface active normal faults offsetting the base Holocene and striking parallel to the thrust belt of the central Apennines, with their fault-slip directions (panel b), and the Quaternary basins in the hanging walls (panel c; Roberts and Michetti, [2004])

pictures.t: Quaternary faults and topographic profiles across the Abruzzi Apennines
pictures.c: Main Quaternary faults (panel A) and topographic profiles across the Abruzzi Apennines with location of the main Quaternary faults (panels B and C; Galadini and Messina, [2004])
